text:
Predicates:
DeadlyDisease(x) ::: x is a deadly disease.
LowSurvivalRate(x) ::: x comes with a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(x) ::: x is a severe cancer.
BileDuctCancer(x) ::: x is bile duct cancer.
Cholangiocarcinoma(x) ::: x is Cholangiocarcinoma.
MildFlu(x) ::: x is mild flu.
ColorectalCancer(x) ::: x is colorectal cancer.
Premises:
∀x (DeadlyDisease(x) → LowSurvivalRate(x)) ::: If something is a deadly disease, then it comes with a low survival rate.
∀x (SevereCancer(x) → DeadlyDisease(x)) ::: Severe cancers are deadly diseases.
BileDuctCancer(bileDuctCancer) ::: Bile duct cancer is a severe form of cancer.
∀x (Cholangiocarcinoma(x) → BileDuctCancer(x)) ::: All Cholangiocarcinoma is bile duct cancer.
MildFlu(mildFlu) ∧ LowSurvivalRate(mildFlu) ::: Mild flu comes with a low survival rate.
ColorectalCancer(colorectalCancer) ∧ ¬(BileDuctCancer(colorectalCancer) ∧ LowSurvivalRate(colorectalCancer)) ::: Colorectal cancer is not both a bile duct cancer and with a low survival rate.
Conclusion:
(ColorectalCancer(colorectalCancer) ∧ (BileDuctCancer(colorectalCancer) ∨ Cholangiocarcinoma(colorectalCancer))) → (BileDuctCancer(colorectalCancer) ∧ MildFlu(colorectalCancer)) ::: If colorectal cancer is a kind of bile duct cancer or a form of Cholangiocarcinoma, then colorectal cancer is a kind of bile duct cancer and a kind of mild flu.
